lenders.name: Standard Insurance Company (StanCorp Mortgage Investors)
lenders.parent_or_aka: The Standard / StanCorp Financial Group; owned by Meiji Yasuda Life since 2016
lenders.broker_program: Correspondent / mortgage-banker channel. Gantry (a California mortgage banker) names StanCorp Mortgage Investors as its first, long-standing correspondent lender relationship, and Professional Mortgage was appointed a StanCorp commercial mortgage correspondent (undated trade item). The Standard's own material describes small fixed-rate commercial mortgage loans, each individually underwritten: an $8.83B portfolio of about 5,700 loans, average about $1.5M (12/31/2022). A third-party profile gives a $250K-$5M range. The Sept 2025 press release confirms the mortgage unit is active. Whether it accepts loans directly from brokers who are not correspondents is unconfirmed.
lenders.contact_title: Senior Vice President and Managing Director (StanCorp Mortgage Investors / StanCorp Real Estate), per Sept 2025 press release
lenders.fit_notes: The life company most closely matched to Corin's deal sizes (average loan about $1.5M), with California historically its largest state exposure (26.2% of the book in its last public 10-Q, 2015). Reach it through a correspondent such as Gantry, or ask StanCorp whether it takes direct broker submissions.

lenders.name: American National Insurance Company (Mortgage Loan & Real Estate Investments)
lenders.parent_or_aka: American National; acquired by Brookfield Reinsurance (now Brookfield Wealth Solutions) in 2022
lenders.property_types: Multiple CRE property types (portfolio over $5.5B per job postings)
lenders.programs: Commercial mortgage loans, Real estate investments
lenders.broker_program: Not documented. The Mortgage Loan and Real Estate Investments (MLRE) team produces and underwrites mortgage loans for American National and its affiliates (portfolio over $7B). No published correspondent list or broker page was found. traded.co shows 3 financed deals (about $188M), most recent dated June 30, 2026, so the lender is active.
lenders.fit_notes: Large in-house life company mortgage team with its own origination. Broker or correspondent access and California activity are unconfirmed, so call the MLRE group to ask how they source loans.

lenders.name: Protective Life Insurance Company (Commercial Mortgages)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Protective; subsidiary of Dai-ichi Life Holdings
lenders.property_types: Multifamily, Industrial, Grocery-anchored retail, Medical office
lenders.broker_program: The commercial mortgage page has an 'Approved firms' section and says Protective works with a variety of firms across different categories, i.e. an approved list of mortgage banker / broker firms. Deploys roughly $1.5B a year in CRE debt.
lenders.fit_notes: Published, broker-friendly box ($3M-$50M, 75% LTV, 1.20x DSCR) and an approved-firm program. A small broker should ask to be added to the approved list or co-broker with a listed firm. California activity not confirmed in search results.

lenders.name: Symetra Life Insurance Company (Commercial Mortgage Loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Symetra Investment Management; subsidiary of Sumitomo Life
lenders.footprint: National; traded.co lists 14 financed deals (about $219M) in California
lenders.property_types: Retail, Light industrial / Warehouse, Office, Multifamily, Single-tenant, Owner-occupied
lenders.programs: Permanent loans on completed (stabilized) commercial and multifamily properties
lenders.term: 10-yr and 15-yr fixed seen on CA deals
lenders.broker_program: Lends through mortgage bankers (correspondents), not brokers, per Symetra's own page; most loans $1M-$10M, completed properties only. California deals arranged by independent and correspondent intermediaries: $16M Fontana, CA retail refinance with broker Michael Kaplan (President, Slatt Capital); $8M 10-yr fixed refinance of Pointe Red Hill office, Tustin, CA, arranged by Walker & Dunlop; $1.4M 15-yr fixed (4.09%) refinance on 7617 South Broadway, Los Angeles (Apr 2022); $31.5M acquisition loan on the PacMutual office campus, Los Angeles. traded.co: 14 financed CA deals (about $219M).
lenders.fit_notes: The most reachable life company in this set for California small-balance deals: loans of $1M-$20M, repeated CA activity, and California mortgage bankers (Slatt Capital, Walker & Dunlop) that already place loans with it. Corin should submit through or co-broke with one of those correspondents.

lenders.name: Ameritas Life Insurance Corp. (Commercial Mortgage & Real Estate)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Ameritas Investment Partners; Ameritas Mutual Holding Company
lenders.footprint: National, MSAs of 250,000+ population within regions served by its core correspondents
lenders.property_types: Warehouse, Light industrial, Multifamily, Medical office, Anchored and unanchored retail; others selectively
lenders.programs: Fixed-rate permanent loans, Short-term bridge loans (office generally excluded)
lenders.term: Permanent: 10-25 yr terms, up to 30 yr amortization; Bridge: 3 yr + two 1-yr extensions
lenders.broker_program: Correspondent model: Ameritas says its program connects borrowers with mortgage banking firms and loan originators nationwide, and it lends in markets served by its core correspondents. Analyst job postings describe calling on mortgage banking correspondents. Larger loans considered. Also takes intermediary-arranged deals: JLL arranged a 5-yr fixed-rate Ameritas acquisition loan on a $12M Manchester, CT distribution center.
lenders.fit_notes: Small-balance life company ($1M-$10M) that also offers bridge loans, a useful fit for Corin's smaller deals. Access is through Ameritas correspondents, and whether it lends in California depends on correspondent coverage, so confirm.

lenders.name: Principal Real Estate (Principal Life commercial & multifamily mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Principal Asset Management / Principal Financial Group
lenders.property_types: Well-leased income-producing CRE: Multifamily, Industrial, Retail, Office
lenders.programs: Core commercial & multifamily first-lien private mortgage loans (life company balance sheet and institutional accounts)
lenders.broker_program: Not documented in search results. Principal's own CML page says deal sizes run from under $10M to over $100M per transaction, on first liens against well-leased income-producing properties. No correspondent list found. California activity: Principal Life provided a $42M loan on a Culver City mixed-use property (2021, per traded.co).
lenders.fit_notes: Large life company lender for stabilized core assets. The way it sources loans (direct or through correspondents) was not confirmed, so a small broker would likely reach it through a mortgage banker correspondent.

lenders.name: Argentic Real Estate Finance
lenders.parent_or_aka: Argentic Investment Management affiliate
lenders.broker_program: Takes deals from independent intermediaries in California: traded.co records a $102M cash-out refinance of a new industrial building in Hemet, CA secured by Ty Newland of Newland Capital (an independent intermediary), co-lent by Citi and Argentic (Argentic lender contact named as Judah Samter). Also a $50M refinance of a Cupertino, CA office asset. Active 2025 CMBS loan seller (AREF2 appears in BMO 2025-5C12; Form ABS-15G filings), about $4.2B of volume in the 12 months to Dec 2025 per a third-party tracker. Earlier California example: $214.8M 10-yr fixed loan on 14 SoCal retail assets (2019).
lenders.fit_notes: Independent conduit lender with several broker-arranged California loans, and it co-lends with bank conduits on larger deals. Best for stabilized CA retail, office or industrial refinances that need fixed-rate non-recourse conduit debt.

lenders.name: Pacific Life Insurance Company (Real Estate Investments / commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Pacific Life; Pacific Mutual Holding Company
lenders.programs: Long-term fixed-rate permanent loans (including on assets still in lease-up), Commercial mortgage loans (balance sheet)
lenders.broker_program: No published broker program. Takes intermediary-arranged deals: JLL Capital Markets arranged a $345M long-term fixed-rate Pacific Life refinance of Miro (630 units, downtown San Jose) while the property was still in lease-up (2022). FY2025 statutory filings show about $17.7B of commercial mortgage loans. The largest single loan at the Pacific Life & Annuity affiliate was $33M.
lenders.fit_notes: California-headquartered life company that lends in the state and will fund assets still in lease-up. Placements seen are through large intermediaries and its small-loan appetite is unconfirmed, so call the real estate investments group.

lenders.name: Securian Financial (Minnesota Life commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Minnesota Life Insurance Company; loans managed and serviced by Securian Asset Management
lenders.property_types: Industrial, Multifamily, Retail, Office, Other general-purpose income-producing (no construction, land, condo or mezz)
lenders.programs: Permanent commercial mortgage loans on general-purpose income-producing properties
lenders.broker_program: Not documented in search results. FY2025 filings show a $5.71B commercial mortgage book (largest classes: industrial about $1.65B, apartments about $1.56B). Third-party tracker shows about 1,283 recorded mortgages (about $811M) in the 12 months to Dec 2025, average about $8.2M.
lenders.fit_notes: Mid-size life company with a moderate average loan size (about $8M) suited to the deals Corin arranges. Whether it takes loans directly or through correspondents is unconfirmed, so ask Securian Asset Management.

lenders.name: PPM America (Jackson National Life commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Investment manager for Jackson National Life Insurance Company (Jackson Financial Inc.)
lenders.programs: Non-recourse fixed-rate permanent commercial mortgage loans
lenders.broker_program: Takes deals from independent intermediaries. In July 2026 Slatt Capital (independent Northern California mortgage banker, originator Jeff Glenn) arranged a $21M non-recourse 10-yr permanent loan from PPM America on a 213-unit Novato, CA apartment property. Trade profile gives a typical $7M-$40M range across office, retail, multifamily, industrial and hotel.
lenders.fit_notes: 2026 life company lending in California arranged by an independent mortgage banker, with a $7M-$40M box that fits Corin's stabilized multifamily and CRE refinances. Hotels are on the property list, which is unusual for a life company.

lenders.name: National Life Group (commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Trade name of National Life Insurance Company (Montpelier, VT) and Life Insurance Company of the Southwest (Addison, TX)
lenders.broker_program: Not documented. Top deals on its traded.co profile include a $26.75M multifamily loan in San Diego, CA and a $15.9M warehouse loan in Long Beach, CA (about $80M across tracked deals).
lenders.fit_notes: Mid-size life company with recent Southern California multifamily and industrial loans of $15M-$27M. How it sources loans (direct or through correspondents) is unconfirmed.

lenders.name: Nationwide Life Insurance Company (commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Nationwide Mutual / Nationwide Financial
lenders.footprint: National (no more than 22-23% in any one US region)
lenders.property_types: Diversified CRE (no more than 44% in any one property type)
lenders.programs: Commercial mortgage loans, including loans under development
lenders.broker_program: Historically originated through a national network of mortgage banking correspondents (24 correspondent firms, per its 1997 S-1). No current correspondent list found. Commercial mortgage book of $9.6B at YE2024, with $434M of commitments outstanding.
lenders.fit_notes: Large correspondent-driven life company. Approach through one of its mortgage banker correspondents. The correspondent evidence is old (1997), so confirm the current model.

lenders.name: Thrivent Financial (commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Thrivent Financial for Lutherans (fraternal life insurer)
lenders.broker_program: Not documented. Audited statements show a $10.9B mortgage loan book (YE2023), mainly first liens on completed income-producing CRE.
lenders.fit_notes: Sizeable life company lender on stabilized CRE. Broker or correspondent channel and California activity unconfirmed, so it is a low priority.

lenders.name: New York Life Real Estate Investors (commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: New York Life Insurance Company / NYL Investors
lenders.broker_program: Not documented in search results. California activity: a $130M refinance of a Southern California industrial portfolio (Sukut Real Properties), September 2025.
lenders.fit_notes: Top-tier life company active in Southern California industrial, but loans run large (nine figures in the 2025 deal). A small broker would most likely reach it through a large correspondent.

lenders.name: Northwestern Mutual Real Estate (commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: The Northwestern Mutual Life Insurance Company
lenders.broker_program: Not documented on a lender page in this round. traded.co lists about 40 closed California deals (about $6B of tracked volume; largest California loan $869M tied to a La Habra property), most recent dated Oct 14, 2025. Tracked deals are commonly placed by large intermediaries (JLL, CBRE).
lenders.fit_notes: One of the most active life company lenders in California by deal count, but large-balance and reached mostly through national intermediaries. A small broker would likely co-broker with a large mortgage banker.

lenders.name: MetLife Investment Management (Real Estate Investments / commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: MetLife, Inc.; also originates for third-party accounts
lenders.footprint: National; regional field offices in Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Washington DC and Whippany NJ
lenders.property_types: Office, Retail, Multifamily, Industrial, Hotel, Agricultural
lenders.programs: Commercial mortgage loans, Agricultural mortgage loans, Loans originated for third-party institutional accounts
lenders.max_leverage: Generally up to 75% of estimated fair value (10-Q)
lenders.broker_program: No published broker program. MIM sources loans through seven regional field offices, including Los Angeles and San Francisco, and its producer job descriptions list mortgage bankers among the external relationships to build. California is 16% of MetLife's commercial and agricultural mortgage book (10-Q, 6/30/2025). Example California loan: $300M refinance on Ventura Blvd, Sherman Oaks (2022, traded.co). traded.co MIM profile: about 50 California deals (about $7B of tracked volume).
lenders.fit_notes: Has local origination teams in Los Angeles and San Francisco, and California is its largest state exposure. Loans run large and usually come through mortgage bankers, so contact the regional office.

lenders.name: John Hancock / Manulife Investment Management (commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: John Hancock Life Insurance Company (U.S.A.); Manulife Financial; loans managed by Manulife Investment Management
lenders.broker_program: Not documented on a lender page. Third-party deal data show intermediary-placed loans, e.g. CBRE arranged a $41M John Hancock office refinance (2016). A third-party tracker shows about $722M originated in the 12 months to Dec 2025, average about $24.8M. California example: $105M loan on 5757 Wilshire Blvd, Los Angeles (2018). A Manulife job posting (Canada) cites commercial mortgage opportunities of $10M and up. Manulife's FY2025 disclosure: 56% of its commercial mortgage book is in the US, with an average US loan of $21.6M (12/31/2025).
lenders.fit_notes: Large life company with past Los Angeles lending. Average loans are about $25M and placed through intermediaries, so it is a stretch for a small broker except on larger stabilized deals.

lenders.name: Equitable Financial Life Insurance Company (commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Equitable Holdings; formerly AXA Equitable Life
lenders.broker_program: Not documented. traded.co lists 10 financed deals (about $1B), including a recent San Francisco loan (2823 18th Street).
lenders.fit_notes: Life company with recent San Francisco lending. Average deal size (about $100M of tracked volume per deal) points to large-balance loans, and broker access is unconfirmed.

lenders.name: Citi Real Estate Funding Inc. (CREFI)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Citigroup / Citibank commercial real estate conduit lending
lenders.property_types: Industrial, Office, Retail, Multifamily, Hospitality, Mixed-use
lenders.programs: Fixed-rate CMBS conduit loans, Single-asset / single-borrower CMBS, Purchases of loans from other lenders for securitization
lenders.broker_program: Accepts intermediary-arranged deals: co-lent (with Argentic) the $102M Hemet, CA industrial cash-out refinance arranged by Ty Newland of Newland Capital. Its CMBS disclosure says CREFI makes, and purchases from other lenders, commercial and multifamily mortgage loans to securitize. Largest loan seller (29.0%) in BMO 2025-5C10. traded.co lists 11 California deals (about $11B of tracked volume).
lenders.fit_notes: Major bank conduit with documented California deals and an intermediary-arranged CA loan. Deals tend to be large, so it suits only Corin's bigger stabilized refinances, usually syndicated with a non-bank conduit.

lenders.contact_title: Director, Mortgage Loan & Real Estate Investment (per WoodmenLife newsroom)
lenders.fit_notes: Fraternal life insurer with a national commercial mortgage origination team and a named director to contact. Ask whether it takes loans from independent brokers and whether it lends in California.

lenders.name: Kansas City Life Insurance Company (commercial mortgage loans)

lenders.name: Ullico / Union Labor Life Insurance Company (J for Jobs)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Ullico Inc.; J for Jobs is a separate-account real estate lending program of The Union Labor Life Insurance Company

lenders.broker_program: No published broker program found. lenders.fit_notes: One of the few life companies that makes high-leverage construction loans, and it is active in Southern California. Only works for union-built projects, and broker acceptance is unconfirmed.

lenders.fit_notes: MassMutual's real estate lender, active in San Diego multifamily and willing to lend on hotels. Typical loans are $20M+. How it sources loans is unconfirmed.

lenders.fit_notes: Life company with recent Los Angeles multifamily lending at a mid-size loan amount (about $35M). Broker or correspondent access is unconfirmed.

Deal dates not confirmed. Check whether Genworth is still making new loans.
